beats.text: Forty clocks cover the cream walls, gilt and walnut and porcelain, and every one of them ticks to its own idea of time.
beats.html: Forty clocks cover the cream walls, gilt and walnut and porcelain, and every one of them ticks to its own idea of time.

beats.text: Gold chairs face an auctioneer's lectern. Beside it, a portrait waits on an easel under a grey cloth.
beats.html: Gold chairs face an auctioneer's lectern. Beside it, a portrait waits on an easel under a grey cloth.

beats.speaker: dec
beats.text: Listen to that. It's like standing inside a very rich man's pocket.
beats.html: Listen to that. It's like standing inside a very rich man's pocket.

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: Don't touch anything.
beats.html: Don't touch anything.

beats.speaker: dec
beats.text: I wasn't going to touch anything. I was going to look at the case on that carriage clock. Lovely little lever lock. Swiss, I'd say. You could open it with a hairpin and a bad attitude.
beats.html: I wasn't going to touch anything. I was going to look at the case on that carriage clock. Lovely little lever lock. Swiss, I'd say. You could open it with a hairpin and a bad attitude.

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: You were going to touch it.
beats.html: You were going to touch it.

beats.speaker: dec
beats.text: I was going to admire it at close range.
beats.html: I was going to admire it at close range.

beats.text: Inès pushes her glasses up with one knuckle and looks at the covered easel the way other people look at a dessert trolley.
beats.html: Inès pushes her glasses up with one knuckle and looks at the covered easel the way other people look at a dessert trolley.

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: Monsieur Moreau wants me to say his portrait is a Fragonard. If it is, I say so. If it is not, I say that too, and we leave quickly.
beats.html: Monsieur Moreau wants me to say his portrait is a Fragonard. If it is, I say so. If it is not, I say that too, and we leave quickly.

beats.speaker: dec
beats.text: And I'm here as what, exactly?
beats.html: And I'm here as what, exactly?

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: My plus-one. Stand near the canapés and say nothing in French.
beats.html: My plus-one. Stand near the canapés and say nothing in French.

beats.speaker: dec
beats.text: My French is grand.
beats.html: My French is grand.

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: Yesterday you told the baker you were a croissant.
beats.html: Yesterday you told the baker you were a croissant.

beats.text: A slim woman in a black trouser suit glides between the chairs. An ivory gavel swings on a chain at her belt.
beats.html: A slim woman in a black trouser suit glides between the chairs. An ivory gavel swings on a chain at her belt.

beats.speaker: madame_verac
beats.text: Mademoiselle Varga, at last. I am Solange Vérac. I sell, my dear, and you tell me what I am selling.
beats.html: Mademoiselle Varga, at last. I am Solange Vérac. I sell, my dear, and you tell me what I am selling.

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: Good evening, Madame.
beats.html: Good evening, Madame.

beats.speaker: madame_verac
beats.text: And this tall gentleman with the satchel?
beats.html: And this tall gentleman with the satchel?

beats.speaker: dec
beats.text: Dec Hartley. Locksmith. Well, escape rooms now. People pay me to lock them in. It's a long story with a short moral.
beats.html: Dec Hartley. Locksmith. Well, escape rooms now. People pay me to lock them in. It's a long story with a short moral.

beats.speaker: madame_verac
beats.text: How marvellous. Then you will keep an eye on our last lot for me. It is the only one with a lock.
beats.html: How marvellous. Then you will keep an eye on our last lot for me. It is the only one with a lock.

beats.text: She pats Dec's arm with a white cotton glove and is gone before he can ask what she means.
beats.html: She pats Dec's arm with a white cotton glove and is gone before he can ask what she means.

beats.text: A big man in a bottle-green frock coat taps his way along the front row. The rubber tip of his cane leaves small black commas on the polished floor.
beats.html: A big man in a bottle-green frock coat taps his way along the front row. The rubber tip of his cane leaves small black commas on the polished floor.

beats.speaker: baron_ostrander
beats.text: Thirty years! Thirty years I wait for Moreau to sell me the writing boy, and tonight he puts it in a glass case and calls it "not for sale".
beats.html: Thirty years! Thirty years I wait for Moreau to sell me the writing boy, and tonight he puts it in a glass case and calls it "not for sale".

beats.speaker: dec
beats.text: Evening. Dec Hartley.
beats.html: Evening. Dec Hartley.

beats.speaker: baron_ostrander
beats.text: What?
beats.html: What?

beats.speaker: dec
beats.text: Dec Hartley.
beats.html: Dec Hartley.

beats.speaker: baron_ostrander
beats.text: I do not hear that side. Baron Ostrander. Collector of automata. Victim of Gaspard Moreau since nineteen ninety-six.
beats.html: I do not hear that side. Baron Ostrander. Collector of automata. Victim of Gaspard Moreau since nineteen ninety-six.

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: What happened in nineteen ninety-six?
beats.html: What happened in nineteen ninety-six?

beats.speaker: baron_ostrander
beats.text: He outbid me in Copenhagen with money he did not have. In my own city. With my own grandmother watching.
beats.html: He outbid me in Copenhagen with money he did not have. In my own city. With my own grandmother watching.

beats.text: He unscrews a silver flask, sniffs it, thinks better of it, and screws it shut again.
beats.html: He unscrews a silver flask, sniffs it, thinks better of it, and screws it shut again.

beats.text: A thin man in a white chef's jacket and a striped apron offers a tray of tiny tarts with the face of someone serving at a funeral.
beats.html: A thin man in a white chef's jacket and a striped apron offers a tray of tiny tarts with the face of someone serving at a funeral.

beats.speaker: remy_castel
beats.text: Tarte au citron. The last of the lemons. Monsieur did not pay for the next ones.
beats.html: Tarte au citron. The last of the lemons. Monsieur did not pay for the next ones.

beats.speaker: dec
beats.text: Thanks. You're the cook?
beats.html: Thanks. You're the cook?

beats.speaker: remy_castel
beats.text: Cook. Butler. Gardener when it rains. Thirty years.
beats.html: Cook. Butler. Gardener when it rains. Thirty years.

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: And tonight?
beats.html: And tonight?

beats.speaker: remy_castel
beats.text: Tonight I am everything, and I am paid nothing. Three years of nothing. Butter, sugar, two eggs, zest.
beats.html: Tonight I am everything, and I am paid nothing. Three years of nothing. Butter, sugar, two eggs, zest.

beats.speaker: dec
beats.text: Sorry?
beats.html: Sorry?

beats.speaker: remy_castel
beats.text: The recipe. I say it when I am nervous.
beats.html: The recipe. I say it when I am nervous.

beats.text: A small bald man in a burgundy smoking jacket climbs onto the lectern step so that he is nearly as tall as the lectern.
beats.html: A small bald man in a burgundy smoking jacket climbs onto the lectern step so that he is nearly as tall as the lectern.

beats.speaker: moreau
beats.text: Friends, rivals, creditors. Tonight, a portrait, nine fine clocks, and one lot that is not in the catalogue.
beats.html: Friends, rivals, creditors. Tonight, a portrait, nine fine clocks, and one lot that is not in the catalogue.

beats.speaker: moreau
beats.text: A relic so old that its owners deny it exists. Lot forty. The Ninth Key.
beats.html: A relic so old that its owners deny it exists. Lot forty. The Ninth Key.

beats.text: A murmur runs along the gold chairs. Madame Vérac keeps smiling, but her gloved hand closes on her left cuff.
beats.html: A murmur runs along the gold chairs. Madame Vérac keeps smiling, but her gloved hand closes on her left cuff.

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: The Ninth Key. Dec, the Brotherhood.
beats.html: The Ninth Key. Dec, the Brotherhood.

beats.speaker: dec
beats.text: I heard. I'm trying very hard not to have heard.
beats.html: I heard. I'm trying very hard not to have heard.

beats.speaker: moreau
beats.text: It will be shown at half past nine, after the portrait, after the champagne, after I have made you all very nervous. Excuse me. I must check on my orchids.
beats.html: It will be shown at half past nine, after the portrait, after the champagne, after I have made you all very nervous. Excuse me. I must check on my orchids.

beats.text: He hops down and trots away through a glass door at the end of the salon. Cold air breathes out behind him.
beats.html: He hops down and trots away through a glass door at the end of the salon. Cold air breathes out behind him.

beats.text: Champagne. Small talk. Forty clocks gather themselves for the hour.
beats.html: Champagne. Small talk. Forty clocks gather themselves for the hour.

beats.speaker: dec
beats.text: Three to nine. Here's the bit I like. Forty clocks, all striking together. It's like a choir that hates each other.
beats.html: Three to nine. Here's the bit I like. Forty clocks, all striking together. It's like a choir that hates each other.

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: They will not strike together. Nobody keeps forty clocks to the same second.
beats.html: They will not strike together. Nobody keeps forty clocks to the same second.

beats.text: The minute hands reach the top.
beats.html: The minute hands reach the top.

beats.text: Every clock in the salon stops. The pendulums hang still. The silence is so sudden that someone's champagne glass rings against a tooth.
beats.html: Every clock in the salon stops. The pendulums hang still. The silence is so sudden that someone's champagne glass rings against a tooth.

beats.speaker: dec
beats.text: That's not right. That's not mechanically right.
beats.html: That's not right. That's not mechanically right.

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: Every one of them says nine.
beats.html: Every one of them says nine.

beats.speaker: dec
beats.text: You'd need to reach inside every case at the same moment. Or have set them all hours ago, hands and all, every one put right to the same second, like a, like a...
beats.html: You'd need to reach inside every case at the same moment. Or have set them all hours ago, hands and all, every one put right to the same second, like a, like a...

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: Like a trap.
beats.html: Like a trap.

beats.text: From the glass door at the end of the salon comes a scream, and then the sound of a silver tray falling on gravel.
beats.html: From the glass door at the end of the salon comes a scream, and then the sound of a silver tray falling on gravel.

scenes.label: ch_01_s03
scenes.title: Winter garden, a few minutes past nine

beats.text: Frost feathers the glass roof. Palms and white orchids lean over a gravel path. Lanterns glow; the moon is cold above them.
beats.html: Frost feathers the glass roof. Palms and white orchids lean over a gravel path. Lanterns glow; the moon is cold above them.

beats.speaker: remy_castel
beats.text: Monsieur. Monsieur Moreau. Flour, butter, salt, cold water.
beats.html: Monsieur. Monsieur Moreau. Flour, butter, salt, cold water.

beats.speaker: remy_castel
beats.text: The clocks stopped, and I brought his tisane out, and he was already like this.
beats.html: The clocks stopped, and I brought his tisane out, and he was already like this.

beats.text: Inès kneels by the bench without touching the man on it. She looks at the cravat, the hands, the gravel.
beats.html: Inès kneels by the bench without touching the man on it. She looks at the cravat, the hands, the gravel.

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: He is dead. And not long ago.
beats.html: He is dead. And not long ago.

beats.speaker: dec
beats.text: He was showing off ten minutes ago. He was standing on a step.
beats.html: He was showing off ten minutes ago. He was standing on a step.

beats.text: Inès stands and turns slowly, looking at the room as if it were a damaged painting.
beats.html: Inès stands and turns slowly, looking at the room as if it were a damaged painting.

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: Nothing touched. Nobody moved him. He died here.
beats.html: Nothing touched. Nobody moved him. He died here.

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: Whoever did this did it here, in the winter garden.
beats.html: Whoever did this did it here, in the winter garden.

beats.text: Moreau's gold pocket watch, open in his hand, its glass cracked and its hands stopped at nine.
beats.html: Moreau's gold pocket watch, open in his hand, its glass cracked and its hands stopped at nine.

beats.speaker: dec
beats.text: Even his watch. That's not a coincidence, that's a signature.
beats.html: Even his watch. That's not a coincidence, that's a signature.

beats.speaker: dec
beats.text: I'm going to check the outside door. If someone came in from the courtyard, the lock will say so.
beats.html: I'm going to check the outside door. If someone came in from the courtyard, the lock will say so.

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: Dec.
beats.html: Dec.

beats.speaker: dec
beats.text: Two seconds. Locks talk to me.
beats.html: Two seconds. Locks talk to me.

beats.text: He crouches by the iron door to the courtyard and unrolls the cutlery. It is exactly then that the salon door opens behind him.
beats.html: He crouches by the iron door to the courtyard and unrolls the cutlery. It is exactly then that the salon door opens behind him.

beats.text: A round man in a rumpled raincoat stands in the doorway, a dinner napkin still tucked into his collar and a crumb of pastry on his moustache.
beats.html: A round man in a rumpled raincoat stands in the doorway, a dinner napkin still tucked into his collar and a crumb of pastry on his moustache.

beats.speaker: pichon
beats.text: A dead man, forty stopped clocks, and Monsieur Hartley kneeling at a door with burglar's tools. I left a blanquette for this.
beats.html: A dead man, forty stopped clocks, and Monsieur Hartley kneeling at a door with burglar's tools. I left a blanquette for this.

beats.speaker: dec
beats.text: Commissaire. Funny story.
beats.html: Commissaire. Funny story.

beats.speaker: pichon
beats.text: It is never funny, Monsieur Hartley. It is only ever a story.
beats.html: It is never funny, Monsieur Hartley. It is only ever a story.

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: He was checking the lock. It was locked from the inside. Nobody came in from the courtyard.
beats.html: He was checking the lock. It was locked from the inside. Nobody came in from the courtyard.

beats.speaker: pichon
beats.text: How convenient that the locksmith says so.
beats.html: How convenient that the locksmith says so.

beats.text: He holds out a hand. Dec, with great sorrow, rolls up the cutlery and gives it to him.
beats.html: He holds out a hand. Dec, with great sorrow, rolls up the cutlery and gives it to him.

beats.speaker: pichon
beats.text: You are under arrest. Provisionally. In principle. Sit on that bench and do not explain anything to me about tumblers.
beats.html: You are under arrest. Provisionally. In principle. Sit on that bench and do not explain anything to me about tumblers.

beats.speaker: dec
beats.text: They're levers, actually.
beats.html: They're levers, actually.

beats.speaker: pichon
beats.text: Sit.
beats.html: Sit.

beats.text: The guests have been herded back among the silent clocks. Two officers write in notebooks. Pichon eats a tart while he reads.
beats.html: The guests have been herded back among the silent clocks. Two officers write in notebooks. Pichon eats a tart while he reads.

beats.speaker: pichon
beats.text: My sergeant has made a list of where the things of this house were at nine. Lemons, chairs, a cord, a bottle. The French police are thorough.
beats.html: My sergeant has made a list of where the things of this house were at nine. Lemons, chairs, a cord, a bottle. The French police are thorough.

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: May I hear it?
beats.html: May I hear it?

beats.speaker: pichon
beats.text: You may not. But I am reading aloud because I am old.
beats.html: You may not. But I am reading aloud because I am old.

beats.text: "At nine o'clock," Pichon reads, "either the curtain cord or the poisoned absinthe was in the kitchen."
beats.html: "At nine o'clock," Pichon reads, "either the curtain cord or the poisoned absinthe was in the kitchen."

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: Poisoned?
beats.html: Poisoned?

beats.speaker: pichon
beats.text: A bottle of absinthe that smells of bitter almonds. Someone meant to poison someone. Perhaps everyone. It is that kind of house.
beats.html: A bottle of absinthe that smells of bitter almonds. Someone meant to poison someone. Perhaps everyone. It is that kind of house.

beats.text: Inès crouches by the glass door. The black commas of the Baron's cane run across the salon floor and stop at the threshold.
beats.html: Inès crouches by the glass door. The black commas of the Baron's cane run across the salon floor and stop at the threshold.

beats.text: Rémy raked the winter garden's gravel at eight, smooth as a tablecloth. Every footstep since shows, and a cane tip would leave a deep round hole. There is not one.
beats.html: Rémy raked the winter garden's gravel at eight, smooth as a tablecloth. Every footstep since shows, and a cane tip would leave a deep round hole. There is not one.

beats.speaker: baron_ostrander
beats.text: Why is that woman looking at my stick?
beats.html: Why is that woman looking at my stick?

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: Because it writes everywhere you go, Baron.
beats.html: Because it writes everywhere you go, Baron.

beats.text: The gravel raked at eight holds no hole from the cane: Baron Ostrander was not in the winter garden.
beats.html: The gravel raked at eight holds no hole from the cane: Baron Ostrander was not in the winter garden.

beats.speaker: baron_ostrander
beats.text: You see? I was not even in the room with his orchids. I am innocent. Also I am deaf on that side.
beats.html: You see? I was not even in the room with his orchids. I am innocent. Also I am deaf on that side.

beats.speaker: pichon
beats.text: Nobody is innocent, Baron. Some people are only slower to be guilty.
beats.html: Nobody is innocent, Baron. Some people are only slower to be guilty.

beats.text: Copper pans hang over a long scrubbed table. A half-made tart waits under a cloth. The small window is misted, frost at its corners.
beats.html: Copper pans hang over a long scrubbed table. A half-made tart waits under a cloth. The small window is misted, frost at its corners.

beats.text: Inès finds Rémy alone, staring at the range as if it might explain something.
beats.html: Inès finds Rémy alone, staring at the range as if it might explain something.

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: You found him.
beats.html: You found him.

beats.speaker: remy_castel
beats.text: I took him his tisane. Every night at nine. Thirty years.
beats.html: I took him his tisane. Every night at nine. Thirty years.

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: Rémy. The commissaire will ask what you were holding tonight. Tell me first.
beats.html: Rémy. The commissaire will ask what you were holding tonight. Tell me first.

beats.text: He twists the apron. He looks at the copper pans. He mutters something about shortcrust.
beats.html: He twists the apron. He looks at the copper pans. He mutters something about shortcrust.

beats.speaker: remy_castel
beats.text: I carried many things. Trays. Coats. Lemons.
beats.html: I carried many things. Trays. Coats. Lemons.

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: At nine.
beats.html: At nine.

beats.text: "At nine I had either the brass carriage clock or the curtain cord in my hands," Rémy Castel admits. "I will not say which. It will sound bad either way."
beats.html: "At nine I had either the brass carriage clock or the curtain cord in my hands," Rémy Castel admits. "I will not say which. It will sound bad either way."

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: It does.
beats.html: It does.

beats.speaker: remy_castel
beats.text: Monsieur owed me three years. That also sounds bad.
beats.html: Monsieur owed me three years. That also sounds bad.

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: Yes.
beats.html: Yes.

beats.speaker: dec
beats.text: They've cuffed me to a Louis Quinze chair. I could get out of this with a paperclip. I'm not going to, because I'm a very good person.
beats.html: They've cuffed me to a Louis Quinze chair. I could get out of this with a paperclip. I'm not going to, because I'm a very good person.

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: You are a very cuffed person.
beats.html: You are a very cuffed person.

beats.speaker: pichon
beats.text: The tools stay with me, Monsieur Hartley. Tomorrow we will talk about why every lock in your life opens.
beats.html: The tools stay with me, Monsieur Hartley. Tomorrow we will talk about why every lock in your life opens.

beats.text: At the far end of the room Madame Vérac is telling an officer a funny story. She laughs. Her white gloves are folded neatly in her lap.
beats.html: At the far end of the room Madame Vérac is telling an officer a funny story. She laughs. Her white gloves are folded neatly in her lap.

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: Three people were somewhere at nine, holding something.
beats.html: Three people were somewhere at nine, holding something.

beats.speaker: dec
beats.text: Inès. You've got the face.
beats.html: Inès. You've got the face.

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: Which face?
beats.html: Which face?

beats.speaker: dec
beats.text: The restoring face. The one where you take a painting apart until it tells you who painted it.
beats.html: The restoring face. The one where you take a painting apart until it tells you who painted it.

beats.text: Inès pushes her glasses up with one knuckle and turns towards the dark winter garden.
beats.html: Inès pushes her glasses up with one knuckle and turns towards the dark winter garden.

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: Then tonight I restore a murder.
beats.html: Then tonight I restore a murder.

beats.text: The forty clocks still say nine. Snow has started in the courtyard. The gold chairs have been pushed into crooked rows.
beats.html: The forty clocks still say nine. Snow has started in the courtyard. The gold chairs have been pushed into crooked rows.

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: Commissaire. How many clocks are in this room?
beats.html: Commissaire. How many clocks are in this room?

beats.speaker: pichon
beats.text: I have not counted them. I am a policeman, not a cuckoo.
beats.html: I have not counted them. I am a policeman, not a cuckoo.

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: Forty. All stopped on the same second. Open one.
beats.html: Forty. All stopped on the same second. Open one.

beats.text: Pichon sighs, wipes his fingers on the napkin, and opens the glass of a walnut bracket clock. Inès points without touching.
beats.html: Pichon sighs, wipes his fingers on the napkin, and opens the glass of a walnut bracket clock. Inès points without touching.

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: A brass pin through the pendulum rod, on a spring. Set hours ago, and the hands set true with it. At nine it drops, and the clock dies.
beats.html: A brass pin through the pendulum rod, on a spring. Set hours ago, and the hands set true with it. At nine it drops, and the clock dies.

beats.text: A timed pawl! That's lovely work. That's somebody with patience and small hands and a lot of time alone with these clocks.
beats.html: A timed pawl! That's lovely work. That's somebody with patience and small hands and a lot of time alone with these clocks.

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: Forty pins, Commissaire. Set this afternoon, while the lots were being hung. Dec arrived with me at eight.
beats.html: Forty pins, Commissaire. Set this afternoon, while the lots were being hung. Dec arrived with me at eight.

beats.speaker: pichon
beats.text: So the cutlery cannot stop forty clocks.
beats.html: So the cutlery cannot stop forty clocks.

beats.speaker: dec
beats.text: The cutlery can do a lot of things. Not that.
beats.html: The cutlery can do a lot of things. Not that.

beats.text: Pichon looks at the walnut clock for a long time. Then he takes a small key from his pocket and unlocks the cuff.
beats.html: Pichon looks at the walnut clock for a long time. Then he takes a small key from his pocket and unlocks the cuff.

beats.speaker: pichon
beats.text: You are free, Monsieur Hartley. Provisionally. The tools stay in my coat, close to my heart and far from yours.
beats.html: You are free, Monsieur Hartley. Provisionally. The tools stay in my coat, close to my heart and far from yours.

beats.speaker: dec
beats.text: That's the nicest thing you've ever said to me.
beats.html: That's the nicest thing you've ever said to me.

beats.speaker: pichon
beats.text: Do not get used to it. Go and stand somewhere I can see you.
beats.html: Do not get used to it. Go and stand somewhere I can see you.

beats.text: Green banker's lamps make pools of light between tall oak shelves. In the glass cases, brass automata wait: a writing boy at a tiny desk, a singing bird in a gilded cage.
beats.html: Green banker's lamps make pools of light between tall oak shelves. In the glass cases, brass automata wait: a writing boy at a tiny desk, a singing bird in a gilded cage.

beats.speaker: baron_ostrander
beats.text: Look at him. The writing boy. Jaquet-style, eighteenth century, forty cams. He writes four lines of verse in perfect copperplate.
beats.html: Look at him. The writing boy. Jaquet-style, eighteenth century, forty cams. He writes four lines of verse in perfect copperplate.

beats.speaker: dec
beats.text: And Moreau wouldn't sell him.
beats.html: And Moreau wouldn't sell him.

beats.speaker: baron_ostrander
beats.text: He stole him from me in nineteen ninety-six, he would not sell him to me after, he would not sell him tonight, and now he will not sell him ever, because he is dead, which is very selfish.
beats.html: He stole him from me in nineteen ninety-six, he would not sell him to me after, he would not sell him tonight, and now he will not sell him ever, because he is dead, which is very selfish.

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: You hated him.
beats.html: You hated him.

text.intro: In this belfry, Brother Anselm explains, every keeper sworn to the Struck Hour always tells the truth (a knight, Dec mutters), and every keeper sworn to the Stopped Hour always lies (a knave). Which of the three is a knight and which is a knave?
text.t1: "Brother Anselm and I are both sworn to the Struck Hour," Sister Odile says. "We are both knights."
text.t2: "Sister Odile is a knight, sworn to the Struck Hour," Brother Tobias says, beaming at her.
text.t3: "Brother Tobias is a knave," Brother Anselm says. "He is sworn to the Stopped Hour."

beats.ch02.s02.b005: He stole him from me in nineteen ninety-six, he would not sell him to me after, he would not sell him tonight, and now he will not sell him ever, because he is dead, which is very selfish.
beats.ch02.s02.b009: I heard you the first time. I was hoping you would withdraw it. Yes. I hated him for thirty years. It kept me young.
beats.ch02.s02.b010: Dec taps the glass. Inside, the writing boy's pen is stopped mid-stroke, a single ink line on the card in front of him.
beats.ch02.s02.b011: He's stopped too. Same pin, I'd bet. Somebody went round every clockwork thing in the house.
beats.ch02.s02.b012: Baron, at nine, where were you?
beats.ch02.s02.b013: Somewhere I could be seen. Somewhere I was not in the winter garden, as your clever little cane theory already proves.
beats.ch02.s02.b015: It is the only one I give to restorers.
beats.ch02.s02.b016: He turns his good ear firmly towards the bookshelves. The interview is over.
beats.ch02.s03.b001: The kitchen smells of lemons and cold butter. The small window by the back door is misted from inside, with feathers of frost at its corners.
beats.ch02.s03.b003: There's a bit of the mist wiped clear. Shoulder height on a short person. Chest height on me.
beats.ch02.s03.b004: You are not a measuring stick, Monsieur Hartley.
beats.ch02.s03.b005: I am tonight. Who was outside this window at nine?
beats.ch02.s03.b006: The chauffeur of the Baron. He was smoking in the courtyard. He swears he saw one figure in the kitchen at nine, through the glass. Black and white. Then the mist came back.
beats.ch02.s03.b009: In this house tonight, it is two people. A black suit with white gloves. A white jacket with a black waistcoat.
beats.ch02.s03.b010: The chauffeur is short-sighted, and he was looking at his cigarette. He could not say which.
beats.ch02.s03.b011: So the chauffeur's black-and-white figure means only this: either Madame Vérac or Rémy Castel was in the kitchen at nine.
beats.ch02.s03.b014: The police are eating your potatoes, Monsieur Castel. It is a sign of respect.
beats.ch02.s03.b015: Rémy. Monsieur Moreau owed you three years of wages.
beats.ch02.s03.b016: Three years, four months. I wrote it on the inside of the flour cupboard. He laughed when he saw it.
beats.ch02.s03.b017: That's a motive. Sorry. That's a horrible thing to say to a man in an apron.
beats.ch02.s03.b018: It is a motive. I know. I did not kill him. Flour, sugar, butter, one egg.
beats.ch02.s03.b019: Rémy, who set the clocks for the sale this afternoon?
beats.ch02.s03.b020: The auction house. Madame's people. They were in every room for hours with their little boxes and their white gloves.
beats.ch02.s04.b001: The body has been taken away. Only the bench, the lanterns and the cold orchids remain. The gravel still holds the shape of where people stood.
beats.ch02.s04.b003: You've stopped breathing. You do that when a painting's lying to you.
beats.ch02.s04.b005: Something white is pushed deep behind a pot of orchids, under the leaves.
beats.ch02.s04.b006: A white cotton auctioneer's glove, its fingertips smeared gold with fresh brass polish.
beats.ch02.s04.b007: That's a glove. That's one of hers. Or one of the auction people's.
beats.ch02.s04.b008: Brass polish. Fresh. Somebody handled brass tonight with this hand.
beats.ch02.s04.b009: The whole house is brass. There's a brass carriage clock on the lot list, with a lovely little lever lock, which I did not touch.
beats.ch02.s04.b011: My dear, are you collecting my laundry?
beats.ch02.s04.b013: We wear thirty pairs a night. One is always lost. Usually in a canapé.
beats.ch02.s04.b014: There's polish on it. Brass polish.
beats.ch02.s04.b015: Of course there is. I carry the lots to the lectern myself. Everyone knows that. Ask anyone.
beats.ch02.s04.b016: "Of course I had the brass carriage clock tonight, my dear," Madame Vérac says. "Lot twelve. It was in my hands at nine."
beats.ch02.s04.b018: At nine I was being an auctioneer. It is what they pay me for.
beats.ch02.s04.b019: And the Ninth Key? What do they pay you for that?
beats.ch02.s04.b020: For one second her smile stays exactly where it is and her eyes do not.
beats.ch02.s04.b021: Ten per cent, my dear. Like everything else. Excuse me, the commissaire wants my statement.
beats.ch02.s04.b022: She goes. The glass door sighs shut behind her.
beats.ch02.s04.b024: Everybody in this house had a reason. The Baron hated him. Rémy wasn't paid. She gets ten per cent of a relic the Brotherhood says doesn't exist.
beats.ch02.s04.b025: Three people. Three things in hands: the curtain cord, the brass carriage clock, the poisoned absinthe. Three rooms: the library, the kitchen, the winter garden.
beats.ch02.s04.b026: And one of each, at nine. Rémy said the clock or the cord. Now she says the clock.
beats.ch02.s04.b027: Rémy said one of two. He never said which. One clock, one pair of hands, at nine.
beats.ch02.s04.b029: And one of them ended here.
beats.ch02.s05.b001: Pichon has gathered everyone among the dead clocks. The Baron sits with his cane across his knees. Rémy stands by the door, twisting his apron. Madame Vérac smiles from the front row.
beats.ch02.s05.b003: Mademoiselle Varga. You asked for everyone. Here is everyone. It is one in the morning and my blanquette is a memory.
beats.ch02.s05.b006: I am sure of what we found. Now I put it in order.
beats.ch02.s05.b007: She looks once along the row: the Baron, Rémy, Madame Vérac. The clocks say nine behind them.
beats.ch02.s05.b009: Madame Vérac. With the brass carriage clock. In the winter garden.
beats.ch02.s05.b010: The salon is silent. Then, slowly, Madame Vérac begins to applaud with her bare hands.
beats.ch03.s01.b001: Madame Vérac stops applauding. She folds her bare hands in her lap, and for a moment the smile is gone entirely, like a lamp somebody forgot to light.
beats.ch03.s01.b003: Very good, my dear. Very tidy. You would have made a fine auctioneer.
beats.ch03.s01.b005: I confess that Mademoiselle Varga is correct. It is not the same thing, but it will do for your paperwork.
beats.ch03.s01.b006: She turns back her left cuff. Strapped to her wrist is a plain silver watch with no hands at all.
beats.ch03.s01.b007: Oh, I hate that watch. I hate that I know what that watch means.
beats.ch03.s01.b008: Gaspard thought the Ninth Key was his to sell. Nothing of ours is ever sold, Monsieur Hartley. It is only lent.
beats.ch03.s01.b010: Gone home. It went up the belfry of the old chapel by the Seine before his tisane was cold. Three keepers guard it now.
beats.ch03.s01.b011: Three keepers. Lovely. Are they friendly keepers?
beats.ch03.s01.b013: Each keeper of the belfry takes one of two vows, my dear. The Struck Hour or the Stopped Hour. The first never lies. The second never tells the truth.
beats.ch03.s01.b015: That would be telling. And I am, as of this moment, no longer telling anything.
beats.ch03.s01.b016: She holds out her wrists to Pichon as if offering him a lot at a very good price.
beats.ch03.s01.b017: Madame Vérac, you are under arrest. Properly. Not in principle.
beats.ch03.s02.b001: The officers have taken Madame Vérac to the car. The Baron is demanding a taxi. Rémy is sitting on the lectern step, eating one of his own tarts very slowly.
beats.ch03.s02.b003: I will send a car to this chapel in the morning, when I have a warrant, a judge and a croissant.
beats.ch03.s02.b004: In the morning it'll be in Switzerland. Or in a lake. Or inside another dead man.
beats.ch03.s02.b006: You go nowhere. You are witnesses. Witnesses sit.
beats.ch03.s02.b007: Then arrest us, Commissaire. Properly. Not in principle.
beats.ch03.s02.b008: Pichon looks at her for a long moment. Then he looks at the forty dead clocks. He takes a roll of canvas out of his coat and puts it in Dec's hands.
beats.ch03.s02.b009: I never gave you these. I am going to the car to argue with a judge. If you fall off a tower, I will be very annoyed.
beats.ch03.s02.b010: The cutlery. Commissaire, I could kiss you.
beats.ch03.s02.b011: Then I would arrest you again. Go.
beats.ch03.s03.b001: A narrow stone staircase winds up inside the chapel tower. Through the arrow slits, the lights of the Seine slide past, very small and very far down.
beats.ch03.s03.b003: Two hundred and twelve steps. I counted. I'm a good person to climb with, because I narrate.
beats.ch03.s03.b006: I am afraid of the bottom. The heights are fine. It is the distance to the bottom.
beats.ch03.s03.b007: Look at my back, then. My back is very boring. People have said so.
beats.ch03.s03.b008: Lantern light spills down the stairs, and with it the smell of pigeons, cold bronze and candle wax.
beats.ch03.s04.b001: Three great bronze bells hang from oak beams, the great bell in the middle. Moonlight comes through the louvres in pale stripes. Ropes drop through holes in the floor.
beats.ch03.s04.b002: Evening. Morning. Hello. We're not here to steal anything.
beats.ch03.s04.b003: We are here to take something back. It is different.
beats.ch03.s04.b005: Welcome, welcome! We love visitors. We have a great many visitors at two in the morning.
beats.ch03.s04.b007: You are not welcome. But you are here, so you should know the rule of this tower.
beats.ch03.s04.b008: Rule. Good. Rules are great. I love a rule.
beats.ch03.s04.b009: The old keeper speaks slowly and far too loudly, as if the bells were still ringing in his ears.
beats.ch03.s04.b010: In this belfry, Brother Anselm explains, every keeper sworn to the Struck Hour always tells the truth (a knight, Dec mutters), and every keeper sworn to the Stopped Hour always lies (a knave). Which of the three is a knight and which is a knave?
beats.ch03.s04.b011: So each of you is one or the other. And you will not say which.
beats.ch03.s04.b012: Oh, we would never hide a thing like that.
beats.ch03.s04.b015: Then tell me about each other. That much you can do.
beats.ch03.s04.b016: Sister Odile does not blink. She touches the handless watch at her throat.
beats.ch03.s04.b017: "Brother Anselm and I are both sworn to the Struck Hour," Sister Odile says. "We are both knights."
beats.ch03.s04.b019: My turn! I hate going next.
beats.ch03.s04.b020: "Sister Odile is a knight, sworn to the Struck Hour," Brother Tobias says, beaming at her.
beats.ch03.s04.b022: And I say this, though it costs me nothing to say it.
beats.ch03.s04.b023: "Brother Tobias is a knave," Brother Anselm says. "He is sworn to the Stopped Hour."
beats.ch03.s04.b024: How very kind of you, Brother.
beats.ch03.s04.b025: Right. Right. So somebody's lying, and possibly several somebodies, and the floor is made of very old wood.
beats.ch03.s04.b027: The Ninth Key. Where is it?
beats.ch03.s04.b028: Behind the great bell. On the beam, in the dark.
beats.ch03.s04.b029: Down in the crypt, under the third stone. Easy to find. No traps at all.
beats.ch03.s04.b030: It was thrown into the river an hour ago.
beats.ch03.s04.b031: Three keepers. Three directions. One of them I'd follow, and the other two would get me killed.
beats.ch03.s04.b032: Then we work out who is a knight and who is a knave before you put a foot anywhere.
beats.ch03.s04.b033: You've got the restoring face again.
beats.ch03.s04.b034: Quiet. I am removing the varnish.
beats.ch03.s04.b035: The bells hum softly above them. Pigeons shuffle on the beams. Three keepers wait, smiling or not smiling, in the moonlight.
beats.ch03.s04.b037: Brother Anselm is the knight. Brother Tobias and Sister Odile are both knaves.
beats.ch03.s04.b038: Sister Odile's hand closes on her handless watch. Brother Tobias stops smiling for the first time all night.
beats.ch04.s01.b001: The stripes of moonlight have moved a little across the floor. Nobody else has.
beats.ch04.s01.b003: Well reasoned, young woman. I have kept this tower for forty years, and nobody has ever worked it out on the first night.
beats.ch04.s01.b004: She got it completely wrong. Hopeless. Truly hopeless.
beats.ch04.s01.b005: That's the most encouraging insult I've ever had, and I've been to Galway weddings.
beats.ch04.s01.b006: Behind the great bell. On the beam.
beats.ch04.s01.b007: On the beam, in the dark, where the clapper cannot reach. You will need long arms.
beats.ch04.s01.b008: Dec looks at his own arms with an expression of deep personal pride.
beats.ch04.s01.b009: I have the longest arms in the Republic of Ireland. It's on my passport.
beats.ch04.s01.b010: It is not on your passport.
beats.ch04.s02.b002: The great bell hangs in the middle, wider than a café table and old as the river. Behind it, the oak beam vanishes into black.
beats.ch04.s02.b004: I wasn't going to. Now I'm going to. Why would you say that?
beats.ch04.s02.b006: There's a box. Little iron box, nailed to the beam. Lock on it. Of course there's a lock on it.
beats.ch04.s02.b007: He unrolls the cutlery one-handed, balancing against the cold curve of the bell.
beats.ch04.s02.b008: Six-lever, old French, rust on the second lever. Hello, my darling. You're going to be very easy and I'm going to be very gentle.
beats.ch04.s02.b009: The Ninth Key: a long black iron key, warm to the touch, with a bow shaped like a clock face that has the nine at the top.
beats.ch04.s02.b010: It's warm. Why is it warm? Iron doesn't do warm. Iron does cold, and occasionally tetanus.
beats.ch04.s02.b013: Do take your time! Nobody here wants that key back at all.
beats.ch04.s02.b014: We would never ring the bells with you up there.
beats.ch04.s02.b015: Dec, they are going to ring the bells.
beats.ch04.s02.b016: I gathered that from them saying they weren't!
beats.ch04.s03.b001: The great bell swings out of the dark like a bronze wall. The beam bucks under Dec's feet. Pigeons explode upwards through the louvres.
beats.ch04.s03.b003: I cannot understand you with a key in your mouth!
beats.ch04.s03.b005: A fene egye meg. Give me your hand.
beats.ch04.s03.b006: She does not look at the drop. She looks at his jacket collar, the way she looks at one square inch of a painting, and nothing else in the world.
beats.ch04.s03.b007: She grabs it. She pulls. Dec swings in over the boards and lands on her and on the lantern and on a very annoyed pigeon.
beats.ch04.s03.b011: You pulled me in. You. Over a hole. In a tower.
beats.ch04.s03.b012: Say nothing else about heights tonight, or I will put you back.
beats.ch04.s03.b013: Understood. Completely understood. I love you. In a colleague way. A professional, collegial sort of way.
beats.ch04.s03.b016: Brother Tobias and Sister Odile are edging toward the trapdoor, the ropes still swinging behind them.
beats.ch04.s03.b017: We are definitely staying right here.
beats.ch04.s03.b018: And nobody is coming up those stairs.
beats.ch04.s04.b002: A round head appears in the trapdoor, then a raincoat, then half a baguette, then the rest of Commissaire Pichon, who sits down on the boards and does not move for some time.
beats.ch04.s04.b005: Nobody asked you to count, Monsieur Hartley. I heard the bells from the quai. Half of Paris heard the bells. The other half is calling me.
beats.ch04.s04.b006: These two rang them, Commissaire. To shake him off the beam.
beats.ch04.s04.b008: We have never touched a bell rope in our lives.
beats.ch04.s04.b009: We are only humble keepers, and we wish you well.
beats.ch04.s04.b010: I have been a policeman for thirty-one years. I know a lie when it is that cheerful.
beats.ch04.s04.b011: He produces a pair of handcuffs and, after a moment's thought, a second pair. Then he breaks the baguette in half and gives the bigger half to Brother Anselm.
beats.ch04.s04.b012: Thank you, Commissaire. I have not eaten since vespers.
beats.ch04.s04.b013: You are also coming down, Brother. As a witness. A fed witness.
beats.ch04.s04.b016: Right. About that. It's warm. I don't think it should go in an evidence bag. I think it should go somewhere with a fire blanket.
beats.ch04.s04.b017: Commissaire. Give us until morning. You can have it at eight with a croissant.
beats.ch04.s04.b018: Pichon looks at the key, at Dec, at the stairs he will have to go down.
beats.ch04.s04.b019: At eight. With two croissants. And if it is in Switzerland at five past, you are both going to prison in principle and in practice.
beats.ch04.s05.b001: Grey dawn comes through the slanted skylight. Half-cleaned saints and shepherds watch from the easels. Jars of pigment glow on the worktable under the desk lamp.
beats.ch04.s05.b003: Eight hours ago I was eating a lemon tart in a nice house. That's the last uncomplicated thing that happened to me.
beats.ch04.s05.b005: She turns the key under the lamp. Along its black iron shaft runs a hairline seam no thicker than a brushstroke.
beats.ch04.s05.b006: That's not a key. Well, it is a key. But it's also a case. That's a key that's a box that's a key.
beats.ch04.s05.b007: Open it. Gently. You said you would be gentle.
beats.ch04.s05.b008: I was talking to a lock. Locks like to hear it.
beats.ch04.s05.b009: He sets a pick into the seam and turns. The shaft splits along its length like a seed pod, and something small drops onto the worktable with a click.
beats.ch04.s05.b010: One hand. A clock with one hand. Pointing at, what is that?
beats.ch04.s05.b011: It is not a number. It is a word. Old French. Very old.
beats.ch04.s05.b012: She leans in with the magnifier. Her lips move. Then she stops moving at all.
beats.ch04.s05.b013: Inès. You've got a new face. I don't know that face.
beats.ch04.s05.b016: Inès slowly turns the tiny clock over. On the back, scratched by hand, are three more words, and the hand on the front ticks forward once, all by itself.
beats.ch04.s05.b018: Outside, somewhere over the roofs of the Marais, a church clock begins to strike, and it does not stop at eight.

text.c1: "At nine o'clock," Pichon reads, "either the curtain cord or the poisoned absinthe was in the kitchen."
text.c2: The gravel raked at eight holds no hole from the cane: Baron Ostrander was not in the winter garden.
text.c3: "At nine I had either the brass carriage clock or the curtain cord in my hands," Rémy Castel admits. "I will not say which. It will sound bad either way."
text.c4: So the chauffeur's black-and-white figure means only this: either Madame Vérac or Rémy Castel was in the kitchen at nine.
text.c5: "Of course I had the brass carriage clock tonight, my dear," Madame Vérac says. "Lot twelve. It was in my hands at nine."
text.murder: The body was found in the winter garden.

text.t2: "Sister Odile is a knight, sworn to the Struck Hour," Brother Tobias says, beaming at her.
text.t3: "Brother Tobias is a knave," Brother Anselm says. "He is sworn to the Stopped Hour."
